                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Use ent ORM + Atlas for database schemas - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-22, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/how-to/entgo-orm)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Create the database using `sqldb.NewDatabase` in `user/user.go`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'user/user.go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package user\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'var userDB = sqldb.NewDatabase("user", sqldb.DatabaseConfig{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Finally, we'll set up Atlas to generate database migrations for the ent schema.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'First, make sure you have Atlas installed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then, create the file `user/atlas.hcl` containing the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'user/atlas.hcl\n'[39m +

                      [32m'src = "ent://ent/schema"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migration {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'dir = "file://migrations"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'format = golang-migrate\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'format {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migrate {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'diff = "{{ sql . \\" \\" }}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This tells Atlas to generate migrations for the ent schema, and to output them to the `migrations` directory.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Generate the migration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'atlas migrate diff $MIGRATION_NAME --env local --dev-url "$(encore db conn-uri --shadow $DB_NAME)&search_path=public"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Finally, make the script executable, and generate our first migration:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Use Atlas + GORM for database migrations - Encore\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-05, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/how-to/atlas-gorm)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then, in the service that you want to use GORM for, add the `*gorm.DB` as a dependency\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Finally, create the `migrations` directory inside the `blog` directory if it doesn't already exist.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is where Atlas will put your database migrations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To wrap things up, let's create a script to automate the process of generating migrations:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'blog/scripts/generate-migration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#!/bin/bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'set -eu\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DB_NAME=blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'MIGRATION_NAME=${1:-}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SCRIPT_DIR=$( cd -- "$( dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" &> /dev/null && pwd )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Reset the shadow database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore db reset --shadow $DB_NAME\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# so configure the Encore runtime to be aware that this is expected.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export ENCORERUNTIME_NOPANIC=1\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Generate the migration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'atlas migrate diff $MIGRATION_NAME --env local --dev-url "$(encore db conn-uri --shadow $DB_NAME)&search_path=public"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Finally let's make the script executable, and generate our first migration:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ chmod +x blog/scripts/generate-migration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ cd blog && ./scripts/generate-migration init\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building a Type-Safe Microservices Backend in Go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-11-13, last updated: 2025-10-05, [Read more](https://dev.to/encore/building-a-type-safe-microservices-backend-in-go-198k)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore treats SQL databases as logical resources and natively supports **PostgreSQL** databases.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a database, import `encore.dev/storage/sqldb` and call `sqldb.NewDatabase`, assigning the result to a package-level variable.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'To start using the database, you only need to define the schema by creating a migration file.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Migrations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### File Structure\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'user/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'└── migrations/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'├── 1_create_users.up.sql\n'[39m +
                      [32m'├── 2_add_posts.up.sql\n'[39m +
                      [32m'└── 3_add_indexes.up.sql\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Naming Convention\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Start with a number (1, 2, etc.)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Followed by underscore and description\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- End with `.up.sql`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Numbers must be sequential\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Example Migration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```sql\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-- migrations/1_create_users.up.sql\n'[39m +
                      [32m'CREATE TABLE users (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name TEXT NOT NULL,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```go\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Email string `sql:"email"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Name string `sql:"name"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'CreatedAt time.Time `sql:"created_at"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Columns: id, email, name, created_at\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Defining Type-Safe APIs - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-28, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the `//encore:api` annotation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore.dev - Go Packages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-10, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/encore.dev)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to Build a REST API with Go in 2026 - Complete Guide\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-02-22, last updated: 2026-06-19, [Read more](https://encore.dev/articles/build-rest-api-go-2026)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Test it by making a request.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The endpoint automatically parses the path parameter and returns JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A few things to notice about the Go patterns here.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters like `:id` are passed as function arguments, and the PATCH endpoint takes both a path parameter (`id`) and a request body (`*UpdateTaskRequest`).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/tasks \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +

                      [32m'# List tasks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl http://localhost:4000/tasks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Get a specific task (use the ID from create response)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl http://localhost:4000/tasks/<task-id>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Update a task\n'[39m +

                      [32m'-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +

                      [32m'# Delete a task\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -X DELETE http://localhost:4000/tasks/<task-id>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to build a REST API — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-30, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/tutorials/rest-api)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Now let's create a new `url` service.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"🥐 In your application's root folder, create a new folder `url` and create a new file `url.go` that looks like this:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Shorten shortens a URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public method=POST path=/url\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Shorten(ctx context.Context, p *ShortenParams) (*URL, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'url/url.go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Get retrieves the original URL for the id.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public method=GET path=/url/:id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*URL, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'u := &URL{ID: id}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'err := db.QueryRow(ctx, `\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT original_url FROM url\n'[39m +
                      [32m'WHERE id = $1\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`, id).Scan(&u.URL)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return u, err\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore uses the `path=/url/:id` syntax to represent a path with a parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `id` name corresponds to the parameter name in the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case it is of type `string`, but you can also use other built-in types like `int` or `bool` if you want to restrict the values.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining type-safe TypeScript APIs with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For `GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE` requests, parameters are read from the query string by default, since those HTTP methods\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do not support request bodies.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For other HTTP methods (that do support request bodies), parameters are by default read from the HTTP request body as JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the API Options in `api` call.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore parses the incoming request URL and makes sure it matches the type of the parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The last segment of the path\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can be parsed as a wildcard parameter by using `*name` with a matching function parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each path parameter (whether a single segment like `:name` or a wildcard parameter like `*name`) must have\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a matching field in the request data type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getBlogPost = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "GET", path: "/blog/:id/*path" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (params: {id: number; path: string}): Promise<BlogPost> {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Use id and path to query database...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m')'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Request validation with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/validation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For `GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE` requests, parameters are read and validated from the query string by default, since those HTTP methods do not support request bodies.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For those methods, the `Query` type is not necessary:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Dynamic path parameters are also defined in the request schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The parameter will be parsed from the request URL and made available in the request object:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Request {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Required path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Parsed from the request URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const myEndpoint = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, method: "POST", path: "/user/:id" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({ id }: Request) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also use the `number` type for path parameters:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Request {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id: number;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts will then try to parse the path parameter as a number.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the path parameter is not a valid number, Encore will return a `400` Bad Request response.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Request {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Required path parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Parsed from the request URL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id: number;'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Receive regular HTTP requests\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-30, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/how-to/http-requests)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a raw endpoint, change the `//encore:api` annotation and function signature like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Webhook receives incoming webhooks from Some Service That Sends Webhooks.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'operate on the raw HTTP request ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Reading path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Sometimes webhooks have information in the path that you may be interested in retrieving or validating.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do so, define the path with a path parameter, and then use `encore.CurrentRequest` to access the path parameters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"encore.dev"\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook/:id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id := encore.CurrentRequest().PathParams.Get("id")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Do something with id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore-api - Skill - Smithery\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-12-13, last updated: 2026-04-23, [Read more](https://smithery.ai/skills/encoredev/encore-api)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createUser = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "POST", path: "/users", expose: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## API Options\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Option|Type|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|--|--|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`method`|string|HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`path`|string|URL path, supports `:param` and `*wildcard`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createUser = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "POST", path: "/users", expose: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const deleteUser = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "DELETE", path: "/users/:id", expose: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (req: DeleteRequest): Promise<void> => { ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Path Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Path: "/users/:id"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface GetUserRequest {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id: string; // Automatically mapped from :id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Path Syntax\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `*path` - Standard wildcard: matches all paths under the prefix (e.g., `/static/*path`)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `!path` - Fallback routing: serves static files at domain root without conflicting with other API endpoints.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use this for SPAs where unmatched routes should serve `index.html`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# RESTful API support\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-07-09, last updated: 2025-07-21, [Read more](https://encore.dev/changelog/v0.16.2)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defining APIs can now include the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`path=/foo/bar` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`method=FOO` parameters to customize the HTTP path and method the API is exposed at:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Order struct { /* ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/ }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public path=/orders method=POST\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func CreateOrder(ctx context.Context, p *CreateOrderParams) (*Order, error) { /* ...```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also define custom API path parameters such as\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`path=/orders/:id`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you specify a parameter, Encore passes that parameter directly to your function as a separate argument, like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Order struct { /* ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/ }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public path=/orders/:id method=GET\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Defining Type-Safe APIs - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-28, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the `//encore:api` annotation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore parses the incoming request URL and makes sure it matches the type of the parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The last segment of the path\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can be parsed as a wildcard parameter by using `*name` with a matching function parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Body parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore will default to reading request parameters from the body (as JSON) for all HTTP methods except `GET`, `HEAD` or\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`DELETE`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The name of the body parameter defaults to the field name, but can be overridden by the\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, the data is parsed as a JSON body for incoming requests:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The above endpoint expects incoming requests to look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Params\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Dynamic path parameters are also defined in the request schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The parameter will be parsed from the request URL and made available in the request object:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'id: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const myEndpoint = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, method: "POST", path: "/user/:id" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({ id }: Request) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Getting Started with Encore.go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-26, last updated: 2025-10-07, [Read more](https://dev.to/eminetto/getting-started-with-encorego-3pk2)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'type AuthParams struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Email string `json:"email"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Password string `json:"password"`\n'[39m +

                      [32m'//encore:api public method=POST path=/v1/auth\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ValidateTokenParams are the parameters to the ValidateToken method\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Token string `json:"token"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public method=POST path=/v1/validate-token\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This declaration tells the framework that this is a public API (we'll see more about this in the following parts of this series) whose path is\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'/v1/auth\n'[39m +

                      [32m'POST\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An API is a function that receives a context and a parameter struct (in this case,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'AuthParams\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'One of the interesting features of the framework is the ease of accessing the parameter values: we can use the values ​​as\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining type-safe TypeScript APIs with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Query parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For `GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE` requests, parameters are read from the query string by default, since those HTTP methods\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do not support request bodies.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For other HTTP methods (that do support request bodies), parameters are by default read from the HTTP request body as JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In those cases, the `Query` type can be used to specify that a field should be parsed from the query string instead.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Params {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'limit: Query<number>; // always a query parameter\n'[39m +
                      [32m'author: string; // query if GET, HEAD or DELETE, otherwise body parameter\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Path parameters are specified by the `path` field in the API Options in `api` call.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To specify a placeholder variable, use `:name` and add a function parameter with the same name to the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore parses the incoming request URL and makes sure it matches the type of the parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The last segment of the path\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can be parsed as a wildcard parameter by using `*name` with a matching function parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each path parameter (whether a single segment like `:name` or a wildcard parameter like `*name`) must have\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a matching field in the request data type.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to build a REST API — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-30, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/tutorials/rest-api)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"🥐 In your application's root folder, create a new folder `url` and create a new file `url.go` that looks like this:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ID string // short-form URL id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type ShortenParams struct {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL string // the URL to shorten\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🥐 Next, go back to the `url/url.go` file and import the `encore.dev/storage/sqldb` package by modifying the import statement to become:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Get retrieves the original URL for the id.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public method=GET path=/url/:id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*URL, error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'u := &URL{ID: id}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'err := db.QueryRow(ctx, `\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SELECT original_url FROM url\n'[39m +
                      [32m'WHERE id = $1\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`, id).Scan(&u.URL)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return u, err\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore uses the `path=/url/:id` syntax to represent a path with a parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `id` name corresponds to the parameter name in the function signature.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case it is of type `string`, but you can also use other built-in types like `int` or `bool` if you want to restrict the values.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Receive regular HTTP requests\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-30, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/how-to/http-requests)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a raw endpoint, change the `//encore:api` annotation and function signature like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Webhook receives incoming webhooks from Some Service That Sends Webhooks.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'operate on the raw HTTP request ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Reading path parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Sometimes webhooks have information in the path that you may be interested in retrieving or validating.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do so, define the path with a path parameter, and then use `encore.CurrentRequest` to access the path parameters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"encore.dev"\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook/:id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id := encore.CurrentRequest().PathParams.Get("id")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Do something with id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Creating an API with authentication using Encore.go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-02-22, last updated: 2026-06-14, [Read more](https://eltonminetto.dev/en/post/2025-02-22-intro-encore-part-2/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The first step is to create a new directory to organize the code:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using SQL databases for your backend application - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-18, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/databases)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a database, import `encore.dev/storage/sqldb` and call `sqldb.NewDatabase`, assigning the result to a package-level variable.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To query a database in your application, you similarly need to import `encore.dev/storage/sqldb` in your service package or sub-package.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, to read a single todo item in the example schema above, we can use `sqldb.QueryRow`:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-07-23, [Read more](https://encore.dev/guide/go.mod)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Go 模块化管理\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-19, last updated: 2024-11-04, [Read more](https://www.acwing.com/blog/content/63608/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'go mod init + “xx module path xx” go mod init命令的实际行为就是在当前目录下创建一个go.mod，而这个go.mod将当前目录转换为一个go module。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'这个 module path 可以是任意的，不需要和文件系统相对应，建议和项目目录相同。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'全面使用 go mod 模式\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. 创建 go mod init +${module path} 创建 go.mod 文件，将当前项目变为一个 Go Module 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'go mod tidy 更新依赖 , 由 go mod tidy 下载的依赖 module 会被放置在本地的 module 缓存路径下，默认值为 $GOPATH[0]/pkg/mod，Go 1.15 及以后版本可以通过 GOMODCACHE 环境变量，自定义本地 module 的缓存路径。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. go build 执行新 module 的构建，go build 命令会读取 go.mod 中的依赖及版本信息，并在本地 module 缓存路径下找到对应版本的依赖 module，执行编译和链接。如果顺利的话，我们会在当前目录下看到一个新生成的可执行文件\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Getting Started with Encore.go - DEV Community\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-26, last updated: 2025-10-07, [Read more](https://dev.to/eminetto/getting-started-with-encorego-3pk2)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To use Encore, we need to install its CLI, which we will use throughout the development cycle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since I use macOS, I installed it using the command:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'brew install encoredev/tap/encore\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With the CLI installed, we can use it to create the project:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since I chose the option to create a project from scratch, the created directory only contains the files with the dependencies  (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'go.mod\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore.app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To use it, let's create a new Encore application with this command and select the `Empty app` template:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore app create\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'encore secret set --type dev,prod,local,pr ElevenLabsAPIKey\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore run\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Install Encore\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Create your backend app from a template\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Run locally\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Deploy to Encore's free development cloud\n"[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you have installed Encore, create your application from the example app using this command:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'encore app create my-app-name --example=trello-clone\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Before running the application, make sure you have synced the project dependencies by running `go mod tidy` from the project root folder.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Also make sure that Docker is installed and running, it's required when running Encore applications locally that use SQL databases.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'💡 With Encore you define API endpoints by adding the `//encore:api` annotation to any normal Go function.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

            [32m'## When to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:\n'[39m +
